description: Six routes R0-13e's route-shadowing.spec.ts found dead behind a parameterised sibling are declared first and reach their own handlers, and each newly reachable handler is proven guarded, scoped and tenant-bound on a real database (k13f_): GET approvals/pending-for-me (was getById as approval 'pending-for-me'; web: fetchPendingApprovalsForMe on app/approvals and app/operations), POST command items/bulk/complete and items/bulk/dismiss (were complete/dismiss as item 'bulk'; web: bulkCompleteCommands/bulkDismissCommands, no screen yet), POST crm deals/bulk/move-stage (was moveStage as deal 'bulk'; web: bulkMoveDealStage on the deals board and list) and GET procurement suppliers and stats (were get as request 'suppliers'/'stats'; web: the suppliers page, the request vendor picker, the procurement page). Guards: each handler carries every guard of its single-item sibling (route-shadowing.spec.ts reads them statically): 401 unauthenticated and 403 for a non-member on all six, and the bulk move needs the single move's crm write (a crm read member 403). Tenant: another tenant's command item is refused exactly like an unknown id (the bulk is all-or-nothing, nothing written, no event), another tenant's deal is skipped with the per-id result an unknown id gets (bulkMoveStage delegates each id to moveStage, the single move's own tenant check, reused) and its row and contact events are unchanged, another tenant's stage moves nothing, and pending-for-me, suppliers and stats read only the path business. Input: the bulk move body is BulkMoveDealsStageDto (crm-deals.controller.ts, BulkMoveStageDto plus a string per deal id), since BulkMoveStageDto let a Prisma filter object such as { not: '' } through to moveStage's findFirst; the command bulk body stays BulkCommandItemsDto; a malformed body answers 400 and writes nothing. vitest emits no decorator metadata, so the suite applies the parameter types tsc emits and two cases read them from the sources. Run from apps/server against a migrated local database and REDIS_URL: npx vitest run test/shadowed-routes-live.integration.test.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-13f-vitest.json, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/shadowed-routes-live.json --report .proof/r0-13f-vitest.json. RED-BEFORE on 87fb3e09 (tests-first commit 17f87369): 14 of 17 fail, exactly the NEGATIVE CONTROL cases (each route answers its sibling's 404: 'Approval request not found', 'Command item not found', 'Deal not found', 'Request not found'; tsc emits BulkMoveStageDto for the bulk move body); fixture sanity and the two refusal cases (401, 403) pass, as the sibling carried the same guards. route-shadowing.spec.ts: 2 of 14 fail (the six unlisted offenders, the R0-13f ordering case). GREEN-AFTER: 17 of 17; the spec 14 of 14 with only the two key-cortex flows entries left in ALLOW_LISTED. Review repairs (two cases added, RED on e321df82, the packet head, GREEN after): the bulk move answered a NUL byte or an unpaired surrogate in a deal id or stageId with a 201 whose per-id error was Prisma's raw message (server source path, code frame, PostgresError), since bulkMoveStage returns each caught error's message; BulkMoveDealsStageDto now refuses such text per id and in stageId with 400 before any deal moves, while a well-formed id keeps its per-id result. The approvals siblings (get, approve, reject, delegate, cancel, escalate) looked the request up by id alone, so a member of any business read or escalated another tenant's request through their own business's path; ApprovalController now answers another tenant's request exactly like an unknown id (404) before any service call, and the request's own business still answers. GREEN-AFTER the repairs: 19 of 19. allowAdditionalCases is false: a change that adds, renames or removes a case in that suite must make the same change here.
requiredCases: fixture sanity (real rows) seeded two tenants with their members and rows; each single-item sibling answers its own bizA row 200 and refuses the outsider 403

R0-13f: each formerly shadowed route reaches its own handler over HTTP, not its parameterised sibling NEGATIVE CONTROL: POST command items/bulk/complete completes the named items of the path business and answers bulkComplete's { count }, recording one 'complete' timeline event per item, not complete's 404 for item 'bulk'

R0-13f: each formerly shadowed route reaches its own handler over HTTP, not its parameterised sibling NEGATIVE CONTROL: POST deals/bulk/move-stage moves each named deal through moveStage and answers bulkMoveStage's { moved, failed, results } (what the deals board and list send and read), recording the stage change as the caller, not moveStage's 404 for deal 'bulk'

R0-13f: each formerly shadowed route reaches its own handler over HTTP, not its parameterised sibling NEGATIVE CONTROL: GET procurement suppliers answers listSuppliers' active supplier connections of the business by display name, with only the listed fields (no credentials or account metadata), not get's 404 for request 'suppliers'

R0-13f: each formerly shadowed route reaches its own handler over HTTP, not its parameterised sibling NEGATIVE CONTROL: GET procurement stats answers getStats' counts of the business's requests, not get's 404 for request 'stats'

R0-13f: the newly reachable handlers are bound to the path tenant NEGATIVE CONTROL: command bulk complete and dismiss naming another tenant's item are refused exactly like an unknown id (404, byte-identical), alone and next to an own item, writing neither item and recording no event; the own item alone is then completed or dismissed

R0-13f: the newly reachable handlers are bound to the path tenant NEGATIVE CONTROL: deals bulk move-stage skips another tenant's deal exactly like an unknown id (the same per-id result) and moves only the path business's deal; the foreign deal's row and its contact's events are unchanged
R0-13f: the newly reachable handlers are bound to the path tenant NEGATIVE CONTROL: deals bulk move-stage to another tenant's stage moves nothing and answers exactly as for an unknown stage

R0-13f: the newly reachable handlers are bound to the path tenant NEGATIVE CONTROL: procurement suppliers and stats read only the path business: another tenant's connections and requests are neither listed nor counted, an inactive connection is left out, and bizB's own answer holds only bizB's rows
R0-13f: the newly reachable handlers carry at least their single-item sibling's guards refusal: an unauthenticated caller gets 401 on each of the six routes, as on its sibling, and nothing is written

R0-13f: the newly reachable handlers carry at least their single-item sibling's guards refusal: a user with no membership in the path business (another tenant's owner) gets 403 on each of the six routes, as on its sibling, and nothing is written

R0-13f: the newly reachable handlers carry at least their single-item sibling's guards NEGATIVE CONTROL: a crm 'read' member gets the single move's 403 (crm requires write) on deals bulk move-stage and nothing moves, while a crm 'write' member's same request moves the deal

R0-13f: the newly reachable bodies are validated NEGATIVE CONTROL: deals bulk move-stage validates its body as BulkMoveDealsStageDto: tsc emits it as the body's parameter type (the type this suite applies); a Prisma filter object, a number or null as a deal id, a non-array dealIds and a non-string stageId answer 400 and move nothing, where BulkMoveStageDto, the DTO the handler had, let the filter object through

R0-13f: the newly reachable bodies are validated NEGATIVE CONTROL: command bulk complete and dismiss validate their body as BulkCommandItemsDto (tsc emits it as the body's parameter type): an empty, non-array or non-string ids, a Prisma filter object included, answers 400 and writes nothing

R0-13f: the newly reachable bodies are validated NEGATIVE CONTROL: deals bulk move-stage refuses a deal id or stageId the database cannot compare (a NUL byte, an unpaired surrogate) with 400 before any deal moves, alone and next to an own deal, where bulkMoveStage's per-id catch answered 201 with Prisma's raw error (server source path, code frame, PostgresError); a well-formed id still gets its per-id result

R0-13f: the approval siblings of pending-for-me are bound to the path tenant NEGATIVE CONTROL: get, approve, reject, delegate, cancel and escalate of another tenant's approval request, through a business the caller is a member of, are refused exactly like an unknown id (404, byte-identical but for the id in the path), write nothing and emit nothing; the same calls through the request's own business still answer
